newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 real GDP seen growing by 6.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 real GDP seen growing by 6.8 pct.

text.p: India's gross domestic product (GDP), adjusted for inflation, is forecast to grow by 6.8 percent in the 1996/97 fiscal year ending on March 31, the government said on Thursday.

Inflation-adjusted gross national product (GNP), which takes into account the nation's trade performance, is projected to rise by 6.7 percent in 1996/97 over the preceding fiscal year, the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO) said in a statement.
Last week the government said real, or inflation-adjusted, GDP rose by 7.1 percent in 1995/96 over the preceding fiscal year and by 7.2 percent in 1994/95.

The government said advance estimates prepared by the CSO in the Planning Ministry indicated real per capita income was forecast to rise by 4.9 percent in 1996/97 to 2,698 rupees ($75) from 2,573 rupees.
The government said India's population was estimated at 936 million in 1996/97, up from 920 million the previous fiscal year.

Newspaper reports on Thursday quoted the Commerce Secretary P.P. Prabhu as saying that the Indian government estimates the nation's trade deficit in the 1996/97 fiscal year will be some $2 billion compared with $4.5 billion in the preceding year.
The trade deficit during April to November 1996 totalled $2.83 billion, compared with $3.30 billion over the same eight-month period in 1995.

Prabhu said the trade deficit aggregated $3 billion at the end of December. He did not give a breakup of import and export figures and did not indicate how the government saw the deficit narrowing from the December level in the last quarter of the fiscal year.
The government was watching oil imports and would be able to firm up its position only in the next few days, Prabhu said.
